ambient_events: Someone's slag thuds off the back wall and rolls into the chalk, ignored.
A regular chalks his palms, considers the ring, and sits back down.
The tally board clicks as somebody drags a nail through last night's numbers.
Iron rings on iron from the corner rig, three reps, then nothing.
Cold air walks in from the bar and leaves again when the door swings shut.
A slag orb is pumped back to shape with a bicycle pump, wheezing.
Somewhere under the floor the drain accepts another contribution without comment.
description: The back of the Sump, and the reason anyone drinks at the front. One low room with the stools cleared out of it permanently, a chalk ring scuffed into concrete around a second drain, and a ceiling low enough that a badly thrown slag comes back at you off the joists. The walls are padded in scavenged mattress foam, gaffer-taped and gone black at hand height — all but the back one, which is sheet steel and there to hit. Along the side: a bench, a bar, a stack of mismatched plates, and a run of sand-filled kegs for the ones who've worked out that Slagball is not a game you win with technique. A tally board hangs where the scoreboard used to, painted over so many times the numbers sit in relief. It smells of chalk, cold sweat, and the drain. Nobody has ever cleaned the drain. Back south to the bar.
name: The Pit
